source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Transference, in which the client's past relationship patterns are redirected toward the current healthcare professional.","B":"Regression, in which a person returns to earlier coping behaviors during stress rather than reacting from past relationships.","C":"Projection, in which a person attributes their unacceptable thoughts or feelings to somebody else in the interaction.","D":"Countertransference, in which the clinician's reactions and past experiences shape feelings toward the current client."}}
source_row.rationale: Countertransference occurs when the clinician's own prior experiences or unresolved feelings shape emotional responses to the client; recognition and professional self-awareness are needed to protect clinical judgment.
source_row.source_detail: Therapeutic relationship discussion distinguishes countertransference as the nurse's feelings or behaviors toward a client influenced by the nurse's prior relationships or experiences. source_row.source_name: Open RN/NCBI Bookshelf — Therapeutic Nurse-Client Relationship
source_row.stem: A nurse develops an unusually strong emotional response to a client that is shaped by the nurse's own past relationships. What is this phenomenon?
